text: Hello everyone. Ladies and gentlemen,
this afternoon we have an unexpected
development regarding the Iran theater.
The U.S. has successfully tested a
directed-energy weapon, which we’ll
call a laser weapon. They used it in
the Strait of Hormuz to shoot down
Iranian cruise missiles and suicide
drones. This is a very effective and
economical weapon. These are the images
released by the U.S. Department of War.
It has been deployed on destroyers. It
has even been deployed on the aircraft
carrier USS Bush. Here is a close-up
image of it. Its turret design is
mobile. This means the U.S. can install
it on any ship they choose. If they
want it on a destroyer, they put it on
a destroyer. If they want it on an
aircraft carrier, they move it to the
aircraft carrier. Because its launcher
platform is portable. Among the many
directed-energy weapon systems the U.S.
has developed over the past 50 years,
there is one controlled by a game
controller like this. If you have ever
played soccer games, you are very
familiar with this controller. Because
its design is so simple, training only
takes a few minutes. According to a
report by the New York Post, the
Secretary of War was able to operate
this system to shoot down a suicide
drone after just a few minutes of
training. Meaning it is very easy to
use. The U.S. military is using these
directed-energy weapons, these laser
weapons, in the Strait of Hormuz to
shoot down drones and cruise missiles
at a much lower cost than other kinetic
weapons like missiles. Now, if we set
up a comparison, the cost savings could
be millions of times greater. For
example, a low-end interceptor missile
costs about 3 million dollars, right?
Meanwhile, a single shot from this
laser weapon costs only 3 dollars. Here
is 3 million, and here is 3 dollars.
The difference is a million times over.
We all know there is a system called a
low-cost system. The low-cost laser
weapon system has been deployed on the
aircraft carrier USS Bush. And this is
a new type called HEL. This system has
been successfully tested and is
currently being deployed on destroyers.
The U.S. is investing another 500
million dollars to continue upgrading
and development. The U.S. Department of
Defense confirmed this week that their
directed-energy weapons have been used
to shoot down suicide drones and cruise
missiles at a cost of only a millionth.
A very, very small fraction. They say
that fraction is tiny compared to
traditional types of weapons. So after
50 years of research and development,
directed-energy weapons have officially
moved from the lab to the battlefield.
Their power can be said to be truly
formidable. Previously, many said that
the U.S. was lagging behind countries
like Russia and Ukraine in drone
warfare. But try looking at the problem
again. The cost of these
directed-energy weapons is actually
even cheaper. Of course, different
weapons require different systems, but
the core idea here is that it is
cheaper to develop. Ladies and
gentlemen, President Trump has just had
another success as the U.S. Senate
failed to pass the bill that would
prevent President Trump from attacking
Iran. It was blocked in the Senate when
a Democratic senator flipped,
supporting President Trump, meaning the
bill to restrict his war powers was not
passed. When the vote count was at
49-49, a Democratic senator from
Pennsylvania, John Fetterman, stepped
in. He voted for President Trump, and
the final tally was 49-50. This means
49 people supported the law, the law
meant to prevent President Trump from
launching a war. And 50 people were
against it. This means President Trump
is still permitted to launch a war as
usual. So, with those directed-energy
weapons and those laws, President Trump
is facing a huge opportunity to
suffocate Iran, especially as many
countries have supported U.S. sanctions
against Iranian airlines. If you look
at the map, Iran is surrounded on all
sides. Georgia has banned these Iranian
airlines. Azerbaijan has banned them.
Turkmenistan has banned them. The
United Arab Emirates has banned them.
Oman has banned them, Kuwait has banned
them, Iraq has banned them, Turkey has
banned them. So, Iran can only fly
domestically; it can no longer use the
airspace or airports of other nations
to fly abroad. However, whether Iran
collapses or not depends on us looking
at China. Because China is still
supporting and fueling Iran's war
machine. With the latest evidence
published by the Wall Street Journal.
China has flown 1,300 flights to
resupply drone components and missile
parts to Iran. That means Iran's
missiles, UAVs, and warhead upgrades
all depend on China. Just imagine,
1,300 flights between Tehran and
Beijing to transport those parts; that
is a massive amount of equipment,
components, and weapons being assembled
. So ladies and gentlemen, in this
state of confrontation between the US
and China, this trip did not yield many
results; it seemed to be just
exchanging gifts. President Trump gave
Mr. Xi a bald eagle, and Mr. Xi gave
the US side two pandas. Danny is
listing the agreements that the US and
China passed during this trip. But they
are mainly old agreements, and there
are not many new ones, as the
confrontation remains tense. Next,
let's move on to some developments
regarding the war between Russia and
Ukraine. We have had fiery verbal
battles at the United Nations with
shocking revelations coming from the
Polish and Ukrainian delegations. First
, I will send you the harsh and fiery
criticism from Poland's Foreign
Minister, Radoslaw Sikorski. He said
directly to the face of Russia's
Foreign Minister, Sergey Lavrov, that
you may kill more people, but you
absolutely cannot win. Mr. President,
please allow me to say a few more words
. Because the Foreign Minister of the
Russian Federation, Sergey Lavrov,
mentioned my name, I feel I must
respond. First of all, he referred to
the 2014 events in Kyiv, Ukraine, as a
bloody coup. In fact, I was there with
the Foreign Ministers of Germany and
France, and there was absolutely no
coup. The then-President of Ukraine,
Yanukovych, was removed by a
democratically elected Ukrainian
Parliament, including votes from his
own Party of Regions. This was because
he had carried out a massacre that left
more than 100 Ukrainian civilians dead.
Mr. Lavrov also claimed, and I quote,
that there is a total ban on the
Russian language in all spheres within
Ukrainian territory. Ten days ago, I
was in Kyiv under Russian shelling, and
I can assure him that the Russian
language is still used very widely
there. Of course, he is right that
ethnic minority groups have the right
to use their languages in offices,
courts, and schools. If this is what he
demands, he should call for the
application of the Council of Europe's
Framework Convention for the Protection
of National Minorities. I do not think
Ukraine would object to this, and the
international community, including
Poland, would support it as well. He
has the right to demand the application
of that convention, but he absolutely
has no right to send tanks and fire
missiles at Ukraine. Thirdly, he called
the Ukrainian government and president
fascist. The elections to the Russian
State Duma have also been criticized
for lacking democratic standards. There
is a way to resolve this issue. My
proposal is to hold democratic
presidential elections under
international supervision in both
Russia and Ukraine on the same day.
Russia is escalating the war because it
is unable to advance on the front lines
. Russia is deliberately targeting
Ukrainian civilians, from train
passengers, street vendors, and even
cyclists to power plants, factories,
and shopping centers. Even the port of
Odesa, which, as mentioned, usually
exports 50 million tons of grain to
Africa and Asia, is also under attack.
Now, Russia is bringing those very same
tactics into Europe. And on the 13th of
last month, a Russian jet-powered drone
attacked a Ukrainian train just two
kilometers from the Polish border
crossing. Another incident followed on
the 17th. Russian drones and missiles
have also struck border areas in
Moldova and Romania. Specifically,
Russia planted an armed drone at the
Leipzig airport in Germany. Russian
drones and fighter jets have violated
the airspace of many countries,
including Lithuania, Estonia, Norway,
and Finland. Russian hit squads have
murdered people in Spain, the UK,
Poland, and Germany. Now, they are
extending their octopus-like reach
across the Atlantic. On the 15th of
last month, the U.S. Attorney's Office
for the Southern District of New York
indicted members of a Russian
intelligence network on charges of
conspiring to finance terrorism,
committing contract killings in the
United States, cyberattacks, sabotage,
covert operations, and military
pressure. These are not isolated
incidents; they are a systematic
pattern of behavior by Russia. The
Russian Federation is escalating
because its leadership is in a state of
panic. After more than four years of
waging a senseless colonial war,
Vladimir Putin has achieved absolutely
nothing. He is running out of both
soldiers and resources. Therefore, he
needs a pretext to declare a
mobilization. His senseless war has
left one and a half million Russians
dead or wounded, while millions of
Ukrainians and other European citizens
are increasingly in danger. At any
moment, Putin could deliberately
provoke a NATO member state and expand
the war even further. Just as the
concerns we have heard from other
delegates suggest. To the
representatives of the Russian
Federation, I have a few words to say.
You have been trying to conquer Donbas
for over 12 years and have targeted the
Ukrainian capital of Kyiv for over 4
years. You have been stopped by a
heroic Ukrainian nation. A nation whose
GDP is only one-tenth that of Russia's.
Remember that Poland's GDP is nearly
half of yours. Europe's GDP is 10 times
yours, and NATO's GDP is 25 times yours
. You may still go on to kill many more
people. But you can never achieve
victory. You can end this senseless,
self-chosen imperial war at any time.
Do not put Europe and the whole world
in any more danger. Stop destroying the
future of Russia itself immediately.
Mr. Lavrov, I know you are listening;
tell your boss that enough is enough.
Next is President Zelenskyy's speech at
the UN Security Council; Putin was
absent, and the stage belonged entirely
to Zelenskyy. First, President
Zelenskyy called Putin "patient zero"
and said he had promised to take Donbas
and Donetsk 18 times but failed every
time. Recently, Putin again promised
delegates from the US that he would
take our Donetsk region, saying he just
needed a few more months. This is
probably the 17th or 18th time in the
last 5 years. He always makes this
promise in the same way. Just a few
more days, a few more months. And then
he pushes the deadline back, and pushes
it back again. This time Putin will
also fail, but afterward, he will once
again make it clear to the world that
even our Donetsk region is not enough
for him. He wants even more of our
cities, from Odesa to Kharkiv and
others. Someone in the Kremlin even
hung a poster with the words "On to
Kyiv." Russia has territorial claims
against our neighbor, Moldova. They
constantly threaten Poland and the
Baltic states. Russia shows no respect
for the statehood of countries in the
South Caucasus and Central Asia. And
sadly, people in Syria and across
Africa also know very well what these
Russian murderers are like. It seems
there is always something preventing
Putin from simply saying that is enough
, let there be peace. There is always
something keeping him from admitting
that his own 17 million square
kilometers of territory, recognized by
the entire international community, are
enough for this man. Putin is always
looking for someone who can help him
kill more. To kill more people per
square kilometer, to seize more
territory, to attack another country,
rather than simply stopping and running
his own country. After all this, can
you even imagine him living without war
? He is patient zero, the one from whom
this idea of war constantly spreads
further. And wherever it reaches, it
only brings pain, instability, new
risks, and of course, new crises. So
the more freedom of action Putin has,
the more dangerous the world becomes
for everyone else. That is why patient
zero must be stopped. He must be
deprived of the space to act and the
space to spread this evil further.
Furthermore, his comrade, the leader of
North Korea, has sent his troops to
Russia to support the weaknesses of the
Russian army. North Koreans are also
suffering losses. Very heavy losses.
You have probably seen the broadcasts
from Pyongyang as they honor those who
have died. And this is also truly
insane. Why should North Koreans
sacrifice their lives in a war against
Ukraine? Kim Jong-un uses them like a
currency, and he gets something in
return. North Korea's neighbors and
countries across Asia have likely
noticed its improved ballistic missiles
, as well as Pyongyang’s much greater
drone capabilities. Therefore, a war
not prevented in time, not stopped in
time, and Russia not being punished in
time continues to spread and sow evil
in its wake. Recently, we brought two
North Korean prisoners of war to South
Korea. These people are not easily
taken alive. One of them, realizing he
was about to be captured, tried to
commit suicide and was shocked that
fate would not let him die. And this is
how they raise people in North Korea.
That is the reality. They strip the
people of their freedom. They strip
them of their right to choose how to
live. And they drill into their heads
that they must die. No matter what
happens, they must end their own lives.
When Russia started this war, they
never could have imagined that our
long-range drones, the Ukrainian ones,
would one day fly to their factories,
their military plants somewhere in
Siberia and on the Yamal Peninsula.
Thousands of kilometers from our border
. Not a single Russian naval admiral
suspected that we could sink the pride
of Russia. Cruisers that were said to
dominate the seas could not survive
against our sea drones. Along with
drones and underwater drones, we also
quickly produce many types of
conventional weapons at a lower cost
than many other nations, all
battle-tested in modern warfare.
Ukraine is building its security so
that we can strengthen our role as a
real security provider for other
nations. Ladies and gentlemen, when
speaking here last year, I said that we
are living in an era where weapons
determine whose voice will be heard.
And I said, if a nation wants peace, it
must strive to build powerful weapons.
Ukraine is doing exactly that, and this
is why for the first time in Russian
history, we are now hearing that their
pride, their oil industry, is drying up
. But oil itself is not Ukraine's goal,
not our target. Not gasoline or diesel,
not the factories or the ports. So our
goal is Russia's ability to fund this
war, the ability to prolong it, making
it more brutal and more destructive.
All of them must be destroyed. Russian
finance and Russian production are what
must be stopped if we want to stop
Putin. And our wonderful soldiers and
our weapons are working on this. For
this purpose alone. The world's support
for Ukraine helps us achieve that. And
I am grateful to everyone, to every
nation that has stood with us, stood
with Ukraine, and helped our people.
Sanctions, support packages, and
cooperation in weapons production. All
of these are important. Of course, they
are very important. All of this makes
us stronger, while when someone gives
Russia more money through trade. They
are giving this war more time. And that
is exactly why we are determined to
limit trade with the aggressor and why
we ourselves are burning down Russia's
revenues. Many of you here, many of you
have witnessed more than once how the
abuse of the veto power at the United
Nations undermines the world and pushes
peace further away. When Russia has
money, they always say no to diplomacy,
and this is also a kind of veto on
peace—not an official one, but a real
one. And similarly, when someone in the
world undermines sanctions, undermines
sanctions against Russian oligarchs, it
may make the lives of wealthy Russians
more comfortable. But it also gives the
war more time, more time for Putin to
send poor people into the combat zone.
Therefore, Russian revenues must
continue to be our target. Yet,
Russia's budget today is larger than
any other year, and most of Russia's
regions have gone bankrupt. Finally, I
would like to thank everyone who has
helped, and thank all those who have
always stood by us, by our people, by
our children, and by our country of
Ukraine. Ladies and gentlemen, we have
witnessed at least five years of such
speeches, but no one has been able to
stop Mr. Putin. So, in your opinion,
what is the meaning of the United
Nations General Assembly? When about
200 heads of state are present there,
yet all efforts to persuade Mr. Putin
have failed. So, what can stop Mr.
Putin at this point in time? I invite
you to help Danny by leaving your
opinions in the comments section below.
I would like to thank you and see you
again in the next program. Thank you
very much.
